method: Direct visual inspection of saved native-art contact sheets and screenshots captured from the actual combat renderer and local production build. Automated results are recorded separately.
findings: Selected locomotion and attack poses retain native image proportions. Extended weapons receive extra transparent space instead of shrinking each frame to its weapon bounds.
Guard ground anchors were refined offline using the neutral/brown soles, excluding the red spear tassel. The corrected contact sheet was inspected again.
Inspected live and matrix screens show HP bars clear of raised weapons and heads. Automated minimum gaps are recorded in summary.json.
Wolryeong's six attack poses show raised preparation, a low forward diagonal cut, follow-through and recovery; the blade stays drawn in the hand in each selected pose.
The inspected WebGL strike and hurt screenshots show continuous sprites without detached mesh fragments.
Production combat HUD fits all three tested viewports; review controls remain visible and direction cards reflow to two columns at narrower widths. The art review page scrolls normally.
limitations: Five native viewpoints produce eight gameplay directions by horizontal mirroring; the apparent weapon hand also mirrors.
Each boss uses one representative attack cycle retimed to its existing skill contact events. Separate bespoke artwork for every boss skill is outside this regional-art update.
Rear-facing limbs and weapons can be occluded or foreshortened. Painted poses retain small drawing variations; native proportions are preserved without frame-by-frame rescaling.
Death uses one drawn pose with a fade. Projectiles, traps and combat effects are rendered by the existing game systems.
The crossbow character's selected artwork places the basket on the right hip, differing from an early prompt's left-hip instruction.
